ac.note: Fake inventory. The corrected figures depend on the ASSUMED COP and on fake operating days and hours.

suggestions.title: Keep AC at 24 degC or higher
suggestions.why: Air-conditioning is the largest end-use that can be estimated from campus data, and the rule of thumb is simple: each degree of setpoint raised saves energy.
suggestions.typical_saving: About 6% of AC energy per 1 degC raised (24 degC instead of 20 degC is about 24%)
suggestions.evidence_scope: General statement by BEE for room air-conditioners; not measured on this campus
suggestions.needs: Current setpoints (a quick walk-through is enough)
campus_evidence: Corrected AC estimate: 143,810 kWh a year (107,858 to 172,572 kWh for COP 4.0 to 2.5), about 29% of purchased electricity.

campus_number.label: Raise setpoint by 1 degC
campus_number.note: Six percent of the corrected AC estimate; the AC estimate itself uses an ASSUMED COP

suggestions.title: Run AC only when the room is in use (timers or key-card switching)
suggestions.where: The air-conditioned site with the most AC hours
suggestions.why: Listed AC hours at the biggest site are long. Every hour of AC that runs in an empty room is waste, whatever the benchmark says.
suggestions.typical_saving: Not a published percentage; the number shown is a formula (hours saved x units x power)
suggestions.evidence_scope: Uses the listed operating days and hours, which are unverified
suggestions.needs: Real hours of use per site (room booking or a simple log)
campus_evidence: Demo guest house: 12 units, 12 hours a day listed, 48,957 kWh a year (corrected estimate, 34% of campus AC).

campus_number.label: Demo guest house: 1 hour a day less AC
campus_number.note: Formula on the listed days and hours and the ASSUMED COP

suggestions.title: Match AC hours to working hours
suggestions.where: The site with the second most AC hours
suggestions.why: Same idea for the next largest site: office-type AC should follow office hours.
suggestions.typical_saving: Not a published percentage; the number shown is a formula (hours saved x units x power)
suggestions.evidence_scope: Uses the listed operating days and hours, which are unverified
suggestions.needs: Real hours of use per site
campus_evidence: Demo block B: 10 units, 9 hours a day listed, 45,897 kWh a year (corrected estimate, 32% of campus AC).

campus_number.label: Demo block B: 1 hour a day less AC
campus_number.note: Formula on the listed days and hours and the ASSUMED COP

suggestions.title: Occupancy sensors for lights
suggestions.where: Hostel washrooms, corridors, stairs and other common areas
suggestions.why: Lights in common areas often stay on when nobody is there. A sensor switches them off by itself, the way malls do it.
suggestions.typical_saving: On average about 24% of lighting energy
suggestions.saving_source: Williams et al., LBNL-5095E (240 estimates from 88 studies)
suggestions.evidence_scope: Mostly commercial buildings, not India; a hostel may differ
suggestions.needs: Lighting load (fitting count x watt x hours) to turn the % into kWh
campus_evidence: Hostel and mess floor area is 3,000 m2, 15% of the campus built-up area.

suggestions.title: Replace old tubes and bulbs with LED
suggestions.where: Wherever old fluorescent, CFL or incandescent fittings are still in use
suggestions.why: Saving depends only on the old and new wattage of each fitting, so it can be worked out exactly once the fittings are counted.
suggestions.typical_saving: Formula: (old watts - new watts) / old watts. No published average is used
suggestions.evidence_scope: No campus fitting count exists yet
suggestions.needs: Fitting count, old and new watt, daily hours

suggestions.title: BLDC fans in classrooms, labs and hostel rooms
suggestions.why: A BLDC fan draws far less power than an ordinary ceiling fan for the same air.
suggestions.typical_saving: 28-32 W per BLDC fan against 70-75 W for an ordinary fan, about 54% to 63% less power per fan
suggestions.evidence_scope: Manufacturer and programme figures, not measured on this campus

suggestions.title: Check water pumps: run time and efficiency
suggestions.why: Pumps that run longer than needed, or run at poor efficiency, waste energy quietly. Timers, level controls or a better pump can cut it.
suggestions.typical_saving: About 20% of pumping energy through equipment and control changes
suggestions.evidence_scope: Weak source: a general statement in an article, not a study
suggestions.needs: Pump rating (kW) and daily running hours

suggestions.title: Add more rooftop solar
suggestions.where: Rooftop and shed areas not yet used
suggestions.why: The campus already has rooftop solar, and its yield is measured, so the existing system is the best guide to what more panels would give. Wind is not suitable here.
suggestions.typical_saving: The Optimization page models solar in blocks; the measured yield of the existing system should be used, not a general figure
suggestions.evidence_scope: Needs the installed kWp of the existing system and the free roof area
suggestions.needs: Installed kWp of the existing system and free roof area
campus_evidence: Existing rooftop solar generated 13,096 kWh in the last 12 months, 2.6% of purchased electricity. It is reported separately and not subtracted from the purchased total.

suggestions.title: Solar water heater, if hot water comes from electric geysers
suggestions.why: Only useful if hot water is made with electricity today. If the hostel uses another fuel, skip this.
suggestions.typical_saving: About 1,500 kWh of electricity a year for each 100 litres per day of hot water, when it replaces an electric geyser
suggestions.saving_source: HAREDA (Haryana), Solar Water Heating System page
suggestions.evidence_scope: Residential figure for Haryana, not measured here
suggestions.needs: Whether hostels use electric geysers and the litres of hot water per day

suggestions.title: Cut unnecessary generator running
suggestions.why: Diesel is a small share of campus emissions, so this is a low priority. Still, testing and idle running can be reduced. There is no benchmark for generators, so this is a what-if, not a waste claim.
suggestions.typical_saving: No published percentage; use the what-if on the Simulation page
suggestions.needs: Reason for each run (outage or test) from the generator log
campus_evidence: Generator diesel: 604 litres a year = 1.75 tCO2e, only 0.5% of the electricity emissions. Highest month: 2025-04 with 77 litres.

suggestions.title: Switch-off routine: lights, fans and AC off in empty rooms
suggestions.where: Classrooms, labs, offices and hostels after hours
suggestions.why: No equipment needed. A simple end-of-day walk-through catches the waste that no meter can see.
suggestions.needs: Nothing; start with a weekly checklist

suggestions.title: Put meters on the main feeders
suggestions.where: The Institute Building and the hostels
suggestions.why: Most campus electricity has no end-use split today. Meters turn every guess on this page into a measured number, so this comes first for any real saving claim.
suggestions.typical_saving: No saving claimed; it makes the others measurable
campus_evidence: Only the AC load can be estimated, about 29% of purchased electricity. The other 71% has no end-use split.

caveats: No official BEE/ECBC EPI exists for educational buildings: every benchmark here is a proxy.
The climate-zone mapping of the BEE bands is inferred from extracted PDF text, not checked against the original.
Built-up area is the brochure figure; a larger real area would lower the EPI further.
No end-use metering exists (AC, lights, fans, pumps), so no waste is claimed from this calculation.
A negative gap means the campus is already below the reference, not that no saving is possible.
